title: Phone Guy's last call
claim: On Night 4 Phone Guy says he may not be around tomorrow and asks the player to check inside the suits in the back room. The transcript marks banging through the message, and music, a scream and static at its end.
quote: Uh hey, do me a favor. Uh maybe sometime, uh, you could check inside those suits... ..uh in the back room? Uh, I'm gonna try to hold out until someone...checks.

when.label: During FNaF1 (year not stated in game)

notes: The transcript marks banging through the whole message, then kitchen clatter, the Toreador March (the tune Freddy plays in the game), moaning, 'Oh no', a scream and static. The wiki matches these to the game's own cues and labels the scream as the yellow bear's; none of that is stated in the game, and it was not checked by ear. That he dies is implied, not stated: the message was recorded in advance (fnaf1-calls-prerecorded), Night 5 has only garbled voices, and Nights 6 and 7 have no call. The quote leaves out the transcript's bracketed bangs.

title: Happiest Day

when.label: Past event depicted in a FNaF3 minigame (undated)

title: The springlock tapes belong to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza
claim: The FNaF3 training tapes are addressed to Freddy Fazbear's Pizza staff: each ends 'You are the face of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza', and the Night 4 tape retires 'the classic suits' in the name of safety at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza.

location: Training tapes, Nights 2–6 (closing line of each; Night 4 body)

title: Phone Guy's FNaF1 messages were recorded in advance
claim: Phone Guy's FNaF1 messages are recordings made before the player's nights, not live calls. On Night 1 he says he wanted to record a message, and on Night 4 he says he is glad he recorded his messages when he did.
quote: I-I'm kinda glad that I recorded my messages for you

when.label: Recorded during Phone Guy's last week, before the player's nights
when.basis: Night 1: 'I'm... finishing up my last week now'; Night 4: 'glad that I recorded my messages for you'

notes: Night 1 opens 'I wanted to record a message for you to help you get settled in on your first night', and Night 2 'if you're hearing this and you made it to day two'. The Night 4 message is recorded on 'a bad night here... for me', with banging in the background. So whatever happens to him happens during one of his own shifts, an unstated time before the player hears it. The transcript marks a bang straight after the quoted words. Wording cross-checked with a speech-to-text pass on the game audio (Voiceover4.ogg).

title: Inside a suit, only the eyeballs and teeth would show
claim: Phone Guy says the suits are filled with crossbeams, wires and animatronic devices, especially around the face, so a person forced into one would die, and the only parts of them likely to be seen again are the eyeballs and teeth, popping out the front of the mask.
quote: Uh, the only parts of you that would likely see the light of day again would be your eyeballs and teeth when they pop out the front of the mask, heh...

when.label: During FNaF1 (year not stated in game)
when.basis: FNaF1 paychecks print the year as 'xx'; no in-game year given

notes: Said about guards, not about the missing children. It is the only description in FNaF1 of what a body inside a suit looks like from outside. The game-over screen shows it (fnaf1-game-over-eyes-teeth). The sanitation clipping describes blood and mucus around the mascots' eyes and mouths without giving a cause (fnaf1-news-sanitation).

title: Game over: human-looking eyes and small teeth in a Freddy suit

title: Clipping: the man was identified on video and captured the next morning
claim: The 'Kids vanish' clipping says video surveillance identified the man responsible for luring the two children and led to his capture the following morning.
quote: led to his capture the following morning, the children themselves were never found and are presumed dead.
location: East Hall Corner camera (CAM 4B), rare poster replacement ('Kids vanish at local pizzaria')

when.label: The morning after June 26 (year not given), before FNaF1
when.basis: Clipping: lured 'on the night of June 26th', captured 'the following morning'; no year printed

notes: Read from the in-game screenshot. The sentence begins 'While video surveliance identified the man responsible and' (the clipping's spelling, as far as it can be read). The man is not named or described. Apart from the five-children clipping's 'charged' and 'convicted', this is the only statement in FNaF1 to FNaF3 that anyone was caught: no call, tape, minigame or later newspaper in these games mentions an arrest, a trial or a prisoner, and FNaF3's newspaper calls the events 'the unsolved mysteries of Freddy Fazbear's Pizza' (fnaf3-coming-soon-newspaper). The game shows the four clippings at random and gives them no order; the numbers in the wiki's file names are not the game's.

quote: Police think that the suspect dressed as a company mascot to earn the children's trust.
location: East Hall Corner camera (CAM 4B), rare poster replacements ('Kids vanish at local pizzaria' and 'Five children now reported missing')

title: Engineers have no explanation: 'never given a proper night mode'
claim: Phone Guy says the first guard reported characters moving at night and trying to get into the office, that from what the company knows this should be impossible, and that its engineers have no real explanation. The working theory is that the robots were never given a proper night mode and go looking for people.
quote: So while our engineers don't really have an explanation for this, the working theory is that... ..the robots were never given a proper night mode.

when.label: November 1987 (FNaF2 week)
when.basis: FNaF2 paychecks are dated 11-12-1987 and 11-13-1987 (fnaf2-paycheck-1987, fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped)

notes: FNaF1 explains the night wandering differently, as a deliberate 'free roaming mode' that stops the servos locking up (fnaf1-call1-free-roaming-mode). Here the company says outright that it cannot explain the behaviour. The complaint dates from the first guard's week, before the tampering reported on Night 4.

title: The 1987 building cannot run out of power, and has no doors
claim: Phone Guy describes the 1987 building as a quirky modern design with no doors for the guard to close, and says that although the flashlight can run out of power, the building cannot.
quote: And even though your flashlight can run out of power, the building cannot. So, don't worry about the place going dark.

when.label: November 1987 (FNaF2 week)
when.basis: FNaF2 paychecks are dated 11-12-1987 and 11-13-1987 (fnaf2-paycheck-1987, fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped)

notes: He introduces it as 'the quirky modern design of the building. You may have noticed there are no doors for you to close'. FNaF1's office has two doors and a limited power supply that can run out before morning, which Scott's store text puts down to 'corporate budget cuts' (scott-fnaf1-steam-budget-cuts). The 1987 office differs from FNaF1's on both points; neither game says in words whether the two are the same building.

title: The older models: 'And the smell...ugh.'
claim: Phone Guy says the plan to repair the older models was given up because they were so ugly, and because of the smell.
quote: But they were just so ugly, you know. And the smell...ugh.

when.label: Before November 1987 (when the older models were to be repaired)
when.basis: Said on Night 2 of the week dated by the 11-12-1987 check, about an earlier attempt to repair them

notes: He does not say what the smell is. FNaF1's clipping reports a 'foul odor coming from the much-loved animal mascots' (fnaf1-news-sanitation), and both games' Custom Night slips list 'Odor' among the guard's faults. The older models smell before anything that happens in the 1987 week.

title: Phone Guy 'loved those old characters'
claim: Phone Guy says he loved the old characters and asks whether the guard ever saw Foxy the pirate. On Night 3 he calls Foxy 'always my favorite', and on Night 2 he describes how the older models 'would always' react to bright lights.
quote: Uh, heh, I loved those old characters. Uh, did you ever see Foxy the pirate?

when.label: Before November 1987 (Phone Guy's memory of the old characters)
when.basis: Said in the week of the 11-12-1987 check, in the past tense, about the characters of the previous location

notes: Night 3: 'Like I said, he was always my favorite.' Night 2: 'Those older models would always get disoriented with bright lights.' He speaks as someone who knew the old characters while they performed, and asks the guard as a member of the public who might have seen them. Whether he knew them as an employee or a customer is not said.

title: The older models 'shouldn't be able to walk around', and do
claim: On Night 2 Phone Guy says the older models in the back room shouldn't be able to walk around. By the wiki's per-night activity tables they are inactive on Night 1, the older Foxy becomes active on Night 2, and the older Freddy, Bonnie and Chica on Night 3.
quote: Uh, those older ones shouldn't be able to walk around, but if they do, the whole Freddy head trick should work on them too, so... whatever.

when.label: November 1987 (FNaF2 week)
when.basis: FNaF2 paychecks are dated 11-12-1987 and 11-13-1987 (fnaf2-paycheck-1987, fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped)

notes: Activity by night is from the wiki's per-night A.I. tables (Night 1, Night 2 and Night 3 pages). The older models are moving and attacking before the investigation (Night 4), the lockdown (Night 5) and the use of the yellow suit reported on Night 6. Phone Guy gives no reason why machines kept for parts should move at all.

title: Night 5: a day-shift position 'just became available'
claim: On Night 5 Phone Guy says a day-shift position has just become available, that the guard may be moved to it once things are sorted out, and that there is no replacement for the night shift yet.
quote: Um, when we get it all sorted out we may move you to the day shift. A position just became...available. Uh, we don't have a replacement for your shift yet but we're working on it.

when.label: November 1987 (FNaF2 week)
when.basis: FNaF2 paychecks are dated 11-12-1987 and 11-13-1987 (fnaf2-paycheck-1987, fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped)

notes: On Night 1 the first guard is said to have been switched to the day shift (fnaf2-call1-second-guard), and on Night 3 the day guard is 'on watch from opening till close' (fnaf2-call3-rumors). That the open position is his is a reading; Phone Guy does not say which post it is or why it is empty. He says it straight after the lockdown and the words 'previous employees'. A 'replacement for your shift' fits the Custom Night's guard, Fritz Smith, employee #03, fired on his first day (fnaf2-pink-slip-fritz-smith). Wording cross-checked with a speech-to-text pass on the game audio (Call 5b.ogg).

title: Phone Guy: 'I'll probably take the night shift myself'
claim: On Night 6 Phone Guy says that when the place eventually opens again he will probably take the night shift himself.

Wording cross-checked with a speech-to-text pass on the game audio (Call 6b.ogg).

title: By the wiki's activity tables, Golden Freddy is inactive until Night 6

when.label: November 1987 (FNaF2 week)

Night 6 is the night whose call reports that 'someone used one of the suits... a yellow one' and that 'none of them are acting right' (fnaf2-call6-yellow-suit). The game draws no explicit line between the two. Before Night 6 the yellow bear does not attack; it is seen in the cutscene after Night 3 and in the death minigames. The wiki reports a very rare Night 2 appearance and puts it down to a bug on the strength of a fan's code analysis; that is not verified here.

title: SAVETHEM's purple figure has a yellow mark on its chest
claim: The purple figure that rarely appears in SAVETHEM is drawn with white eyes, a wide grin, one arm held out in front and a yellow-orange mark on its chest. The purple figures in Take Cake to the Children and Foxy Go! Go! Go! are plain, with no chest mark.

when.label: At the FNaF2 location (on or before Nov 1987)
when.basis: Layout shows the FNaF2 cast (Toy animatronics, Mangle, old models); undated

notes: Read from the sprite and compared with two others, the purple figures of Take Cake to the Children and Foxy Go! Go! Go!; the other games' sprites were not compared side by side for this record. What the mark is (a badge is the usual reading) and whether the outstretched hand holds anything are not stated; the sprite is only a few pixels across. In the capture on file FNaF3's purple figure has white eyes and no chest mark (fnaf3-n5-ghosts-safe-room). FNaF4's back-room purple figure has a chest mark too. In the wiki's capture of that scene (File:FNAF4-PurpleGuy-SpringBonnie.png, looked at on 2026-10-03) it is a short horizontal yellow bar, high on the chest and right of centre as seen, away from the arms held out to the left. This sprite's mark is larger and more orange: a block about half as wide as the torso, broader at the top, on the half of the chest nearer the outstretched arm (fnaf4-purple-guy-suits-up-employee). As far as this archive's records go, this is the only purple figure shown in a building that can be read as the 1987 restaurant.

notes: The wiki gives the chance as 1 in 25 per room. The sprite, a yellow bear with black eye sockets, exists in a second version with white pupils (File:GoldenFreddySpriteDeathMinigames.png and its 'LitEyes' variant, both checked). The figure does nothing and the player can walk past it. It puts the yellow bear inside the 1987 building, in the same minigame as the five bodies and the purple figure.

title: Cutscenes: a show stage seen through the eye holes of a head
claim: FNaF2's cutscenes are seen through the two eye holes of a mask or head, from the middle of a show stage, with Bonnie and Chica of the older design standing on either side and party tables beyond. Both are whole, with their faces and limbs, unlike the damaged older models in the same game's Parts/Service room.

when.label: Undated (a scene outside the 1987 building, shown between FNaF2's nights)
when.basis: The room is not the FNaF2 location and no date is given

notes: Read from the in-game screenshot (File:Chicarechereche.png) and the scene's panorama textures. The room has long party tables with party hats and hanging stars, as FNaF1's Dining Area has, and the viewer stands where Freddy stands on FNaF1's Show Stage. The wiki describes it as the first game's pizzeria; the game does not label it. FNaF2's own older Bonnie has no face and one arm (fnaf2-parts-service-old-models), so this is not the 1987 building as the guard finds it. Whether the scene is a memory, a dream or something still to come is not stated. The wiki's audio table lists a 'machine turn' sound for the viewer's head movement and children's laughter; not checked by ear.

title: ROBOTS SCRAPPED: the new animatronics go, the originals are kept
claim: The closing newspaper says the new animatronics will be scrapped because of possible malfunctions, while the original characters are being kept in hopes of a reorganization of the company.
quote: The new animatronics will be scrapped due to possible malfunctions, however the original characters are being kept in hopes of a possible reorganization of the company.

when.label: After 11-13-1987 (closure of the 1987 location)
when.basis: The newspaper lies under the overtime check dated 11-13-1987 (fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped); the article itself is undated

notes: Read from the in-game screenshot. 'The original characters' are the older Freddy, Bonnie, Chica and Foxy kept for parts in the back (fnaf2-call2-older-models). FNaF1's cast is those four and none of the new ones (fnaf1-custom-night-names). The article gives 'possible malfunctions' as the only reason and says nothing of the investigation described in the calls.

title: CEO: 'we will reopen someday', with 'a much smaller budget'
claim: In the closing newspaper the CEO of Fazbear Entertainment calls the closure a minor setback and says the company is confident it will reopen someday, even if with a much smaller budget.
quote: "It's a minor setback. We are confident that we will reopen someday, even if it is with a much smaller budget." -CEO Fazbear Ent.

when.label: After 11-13-1987 (closure of the 1987 location)
when.basis: The newspaper lies under the overtime check dated 11-13-1987 (fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped); the article itself is undated

notes: Read from the in-game screenshot. FNaF1's restaurant has only the original characters (fnaf2-news-originals-kept) and runs its night shift on a rationed power supply, which Scott's store text puts down to 'corporate budget cuts' (scott-fnaf1-steam-budget-cuts). No game says in words that FNaF1's restaurant is this reopening.

title: Parts/Service: the older Bonnie sits with its face and one arm missing
claim: On the Parts/Service camera the older Bonnie sits slumped against the wall with its face and left arm missing and wires hanging out, and the older Freddy lies on the floor beside it.

when.label: November 1987 (FNaF2 week)
when.basis: FNaF2 paychecks are dated 11-12-1987 and 11-13-1987 (fnaf2-paycheck-1987, fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped)

notes: Read from the in-game camera image; part of a third figure is at the left edge of the frame. Phone Guy says these models were to be repaired and retrofitted and are now used for parts (fnaf2-call2-older-models). FNaF1's Bonnie has its face and both arms, so the animatronics of FNaF1 are not in this state.

title: Game over: looking out through a mask at the older Freddy
claim: FNaF2's game-over screen is a view from inside a head or mask, out through its two eye holes, with the older Freddy's face staring in from close by.

when.label: November 1987 (FNaF2 week)
when.basis: FNaF2 paychecks are dated 11-12-1987 and 11-13-1987 (fnaf2-paycheck-1987, fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped)

notes: Read from the in-game image. The framing, two eye holes with darkness around them, is that of the between-night cutscenes (fnaf2-cutscenes-old-stage-through-eye-holes). The screen fits Phone Guy's warning that the robots want 'to stuff you into a suit'. It does not show whose eyes the viewer is using.

title: The springlock suits walk toward sound, to stay where the children are
claim: The Night 2 tape says that in animatronic form the two suits are set to turn and walk toward sound cues, which it calls a hands-free way of making sure the animatronics stay where the children are.
quote: This is an easy and hands-free approach, to making sure the animatronics stay where the children are

when.label: Undated past (era of the springlock suits, recorded on training tapes)
when.basis: Tapes were found at Fazbear's Fright as 'vintage' recordings; no date given

notes: The sentence before it, as the wiki transcribes it: 'For ease of operation the animatronics are set to turn and walk toward sound cues.' The quote is the clause on which the wiki transcript and a speech-to-text pass on the game audio agree; the sentence goes on 'for maximum entertainment / crowd-pleasing value'. In FNaF3's play Springtrap is moved about in just this way, with a clip of Balloon Boy's laugh (fnaf3-audio-lure-mechanic).

title: The suits' hand crank is 'provided by the manufacturer'
claim: The Night 2 tape says the suits are switched to suit mode with a hand crank 'provided by the manufacturer', which recoils and compresses the animatronic parts against the sides of the suit so that a person can climb in.
quote: To change the animatronics to suit mode, insert and turn firmly the hand crank provided by the manufacturer.

when.label: Undated past (era of the springlock suits, recorded on training tapes)
when.basis: Tapes were found at Fazbear's Fright as 'vintage' recordings; no date given

notes: The tape says 'the manufacturer' and does not name it; taking this as an outside maker of the suits is a small reading. In the Night 5 minigame the purple figure climbs into the suit in a hurry and no crank is shown (fnaf3-n5-springlock-death). Later games name makers of springlock suits; this tape does not. Wording cross-checked with a speech-to-text pass on the game audio.

title: A loosened springlock means 'bleeding out'
claim: The Night 3 tape tells an employee whose springlocks come loose while wearing the suit to move away from populated areas before bleeding out, so as not to spoil the customers' experience.
quote: please try to maneuver away from populated areas before bleeding out

when.label: Undated past (era of the springlock suits, recorded on training tapes)
when.basis: Tapes were found at Fazbear's Fright as 'vintage' recordings; no date given

notes: The tape treats a springlock failure as fatal. The quote is the part of the sentence on which the wiki transcript and a speech-to-text pass on the game audio agree; they differ on the small words around it ('the suit' or 'a suit', 'as not to' or 'as to not'). The sentence before it warns that moisture may loosen the springlocks (fnaf3-tape3-springlock-bleeding).

title: 'We are free of liability, do as you wish'
claim: The Night 4 tape repeats that the classic suits are not to be touched, activated or worn, then says the company is free of liability and staff may do as they wish. Until replacements arrive staff are to wear temporary costumes found at short notice.
quote: I repeat, the classic suits are not to be touched, activated, or worn. That being said, we are free of liability, do as you wish.

when.label: Undated past (era of the springlock suits, recorded on training tapes)
when.basis: Tapes were found at Fazbear's Fright as 'vintage' recordings; no date given

notes: Also on the tape: 'Until replacements arrive, you'll be expected to wear the temporary costumes provided to you. Keep in mind that they were found on very short notice, so questions about appropriateness / relevance should be deflected.' The tape bans the suits and disclaims responsibility in the same breath. The next tape reports that the Spring Bonnie suit has been moved (fnaf3-tape5-spring-bonnie-moved). Wording cross-checked with a speech-to-text pass on the game audio.

title: 'The Spring Bonnie animatronic has been noticeably moved'
claim: The Night 5 tape says management has been made aware that the Spring Bonnie animatronic has been noticeably moved, and reminds employees that the costume is not safe to wear under any circumstances.
quote: Management has also been made aware that the Spring Bonnie animatronic has been noticeably moved, and would like to remind employees that this costume is not safe to wear under any circumstances.

when.label: Undated past (era of the springlock suits, recorded on training tapes)
when.basis: Tapes were found at Fazbear's Fright as 'vintage' recordings; no date given

notes: The only place in FNaF1 to FNaF3 where the name 'Spring Bonnie' is spoken. The tape does not say who moved it or what for, and it does not name the second suit. The reminder follows straight on the rule that no customer should ever be taken into the safe room (fnaf3-tape5-no-customers-safe-room); the tape itself does not connect the two. The suit is called an 'animatronic' and a 'costume' in one sentence. Wording cross-checked with a speech-to-text pass on the game audio.

title: The safe room is sealed with its contents inside
claim: The Night 6 tape says nothing is being taken out of the safe room before it is walled up.
quote: Nothing is being taken out beforehand, so if you left anything inside, then it's your own fault.

when.label: Undated past (era of the springlock suits, recorded on training tapes)
when.basis: Tapes were found at Fazbear's Fright as 'vintage' recordings; no date given

notes: The tape gives 'budget restrictions' as the reason for sealing the rooms 'at most locations. Including this one.' The Night 5 tape says the safe room 'is reserved for equipment and/or other properties not being currently used', and in the Night 5 minigame the hidden room holds a yellow rabbit suit and three arcade cabinets (fnaf3-n5-ghosts-safe-room). The tape does not list what was left inside. Whether the Night 5 minigame, with the purple figure in the hidden room, comes before or after the sealing is not shown. Wording cross-checked with a speech-to-text pass on the game audio.

title: The sealed room is not to be mentioned to family, friends or insurers
claim: The Night 6 tape says management asks that the sealed safe room not be mentioned to family, friends or insurance representatives.
quote: Management also requests that this room not be mentioned to family, friends, or insurance representatives.

when.label: Undated past (era of the springlock suits, recorded on training tapes)
when.basis: Tapes were found at Fazbear's Fright as 'vintage' recordings; no date given

notes: The tape gives no reason for the secrecy. In FNaF3 the attraction's staff learn of such a room only from 'some guy who helped design one of the buildings' (fnaf3-call1-boarded-room-lead). Wording cross-checked with a speech-to-text pass on the game audio.

title: The tapes open with the 'hello, hello' of the FNaF1 and FNaF2 calls
claim: Each of FNaF3's five training tapes opens with a 'hello, hello' greeting, the greeting that opens the phone messages of FNaF1 and FNaF2. No game names the speaker of the tapes or says that he is the caller.
quote: Hello, hello?
location: Opening words of the Night 2–6 training tapes

when.label: Undated past (era of the springlock suits, recorded on training tapes)
when.basis: Tapes were found at Fazbear's Fright as 'vintage' recordings; no date given

notes: Openings as transcribed. FNaF1: 'Hello, hello?' (Night 1), 'Uh, hello? Hello?' (2), 'Hello, hello!' (3 and 4). FNaF2: 'Uh, hello? Hello, hello?' (1) and 'hello hello' on every later night. FNaF3 tapes: 'Uh hello? Hello hello!' (Nights 2 and 4), 'Uh, hello hello!' (3), 'Hello, hello?' (5), 'Uh hello, hello?' (6). The halting delivery is the same as well. That this is one man is the small reading: same greeting, same manner, and a speaker who trains staff for the company the caller works for. The tapes are spoken as management announcements ('Management has also been made aware'), a different job from the night guard's. The attraction's caller says only that they were 'training tapes, for like other employees'. If it is one man, the tapes were recorded before the Night 4 message of FNaF1.

title: Springtrap walks toward a played clip of Balloon Boy's laugh
claim: In FNaF3 the guard keeps Springtrap away by playing a clip of Balloon Boy's laugh through the audio device of a room next to the one he is in. Springtrap then walks to that room.
location: Nights 2–6 gameplay (the audio devices on the camera system)

when.label: During FNaF3 (30 years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed)
when.basis: Scott's FNaF3 Steam description: 'Thirty years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed it's doors'

notes: The wiki describes the sound as a 'sound byte of BB's laugh' and says Springtrap has a small chance of ignoring it. The behaviour is what the Night 2 tape says the springlock suits were built to do in animatronic form (fnaf3-tape2-sound-cues). The game does not remark on why this sound works.

title: The end-of-night minigames are set in a building laid out like FNaF1's
claim: The building of FNaF3's end-of-night minigames has a show stage with Freddy, Bonnie and Chica at the top centre, a room of spare heads at the top left, a curtained alcove on the left where Foxy starts, two corridors running down to an office with a desk and a fan at the bottom, and a dark room in the top right corner holding a yellow suit. Apart from that last room, this is the arrangement of FNaF1's camera map.

when.label: Past event depicted in a FNaF3 minigame (undated)
when.basis: Minigame gives no date

notes: Read from the map sprite sheet, brightened for legibility. The game does not label the building; the wiki says the map 'seems to match up with the layout of the pizzeria from the first' game. None of FNaF1's eleven cameras shows a room like the one with the yellow suit, which fits the Night 3 tape's 'one extra room that is not included in the digital map layout' (fnaf3-tape3-safe-room). The four animatronics here are whole, with their faces, as in FNaF1 and unlike the older models in FNaF2's Parts/Service room.

title: The minigame building is empty of people and marked with dark patches
claim: In the end-of-night minigames the building's floors and tables carry dark puddle-shaped patches, and no staff or customers appear. The only figures are the four animatronics, the dark bear, the purple figure and, on the last night, the grey children.

when.label: Past event depicted in a FNaF3 minigame (undated)
when.basis: Minigame gives no date

notes: Patches read from the brightened map. The wiki's audio table for these minigames lists a track of 'rain and thundering' (Rainstorm2.ogg); not checked by ear. The game does not say what the patches are, whether the roof leaks, or whether the restaurant is shut for the night or shut for good. The wiki's account that a leaking roof set off the springlocks is its own inference from these details and from the Night 3 tape's warning about moisture (fnaf3-tape3-springlock-bleeding).

title: A slumped bear sometimes sits in the FNaF3 office
claim: Rarely, a slumped, eyeless bear in a top hat sits on the floor at the far left of the FNaF3 office, in the pose of the yellow bear of FNaF1 and FNaF2. It looks dark in the office's green light, does nothing, and is not listed in the Extras menu.

when.label: During FNaF3 (30 years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed)
when.basis: Scott's FNaF3 Steam description: 'Thirty years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed it's doors'

notes: Read from the in-game image. The wiki identifies the figure as the dark bear (its 'Shadow Freddy'), while the screenshot's own file name calls it Golden Freddy; in the office's green light its colour cannot settle the matter, so both ids are tagged. 'Crumpled Freddy suit' is a guidebook label and is not used. The pose is that of the slumped bear of FNaF1 (fnaf1-golden-freddy-office-figure) and FNaF2 (fnaf2-golden-freddy-office, fnaf2-shadow-freddy).

title: The office's box of relics holds the heads of the 1987 cast
claim: A cardboard box in the FNaF3 office holds the empty heads of the 1987 cast: Balloon Boy, Mangle, Toy Bonnie and Toy Chica, with a top-hatted head behind them. With them are an animatronic arm, a hook arm, a guitar and a paper-plate doll. An eyeless, empty Freddy suit on a stand is posed in the hall outside the door.
location: The Office (box by the door, and the hall outside)

when.label: During FNaF3 (30 years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed)
when.basis: Scott's FNaF3 Steam description: 'Thirty years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed it's doors'

notes: Read from the in-game office image. The wiki identifies the half-hidden head as Toy Freddy's, the arm and guitar as Toy Bonnie's, the hook arm as the older Foxy's and the paper-plate figure as the one from FNaF2's party room; those four identifications go beyond what the image alone shows. The heads belong to the cast of the 1987 restaurant, which its closing newspaper said would be scrapped (fnaf2-news-originals-kept). The Freddy suit and the Foxy head the attraction's caller mentions (fnaf3-call1-relics-foxy-head) are of the older characters; the caller is not sure the head is authentic, and whose hook it is the image does not show. Scott's store text lists the finds as 'empty shells, a hand, a hook, an old paper-plate doll' (scott-fnaf3-steam-description). Every shell is empty; none is a working animatronic.

title: The newspapers' blurred side columns: Scott's development notes, by the wiki's transcript
claim: The columns on either side of FNaF3's 'COMING SOON!' and 'IT BURNS!' newspapers are too blurred to read cleanly in play. As the wiki transcribes them, they are out-of-universe notes by Scott about making the first game: the broken-down robots in his older games, choosing this idea over two others, a crowdfunding campaign that raised nothing, the characters' names starting as nicknames, Freddy at first not being meant to move, a sleepwalking nightmare about Bonnie, and modelling Foxy on a car journey in the summer of 2014.

when.label: Out-of-universe (developer commentary, 2015)
when.basis: Not an in-universe text

notes: The text is out of focus in the game. The wiki transcribes it, and the first paragraphs agree with the blurred shapes in the 'COMING SOON!' image; no quote is given because the in-game text cannot be read cleanly. One note says the four names 'were just nicknames while I worked on the characters', another that 'Freddy was never originally meant to move around the diner'. Nothing here is in-universe.

title: FNaF3 never names its guard
claim: FNaF3 gives its player character no name. It has no paycheck and no pink slip: the screens after Night 5 and after Nightmare are the row of heads and the fire newspaper.
location: Night 5 and Nightmare completion screens; the calls of the attraction's caller

when.label: During FNaF3 (30 years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed)
when.basis: Scott's FNaF3 Steam description: 'Thirty years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed it's doors'

notes: A negative observation from the game's end screens and both calls of the attraction's caller. FNaF1 and FNaF2 name their guards only on those documents (Mike Schmidt, Jeremy Fitzgerald, Fritz Smith). The caller's first call opens 'glad you came back for another night', so the game's Night 1 is not the guard's first shift. Any identification of this guard with a named character comes from outside FNaF3.

title: Scott: FNaF1's power limit is 'corporate budget cuts'
claim: Scott's FNaF1 Steam description says the guard may use only a very limited amount of electricity per night because of corporate budget cuts, and that it was much cheaper to hire a security guard than to find a repairman.
quote: You have a very limited amount of electricity that you're allowed to use per night (corporate budget cuts, you know).
location: Five Nights at Freddy's Steam store description (2014)

when.label: During FNaF1 (store text gives no date)
when.basis: Promotional text; no in-universe date

notes: Fetched from the Steam appdetails API. The same text says the robots' behaviour 'has become somewhat unpredictable at night' and that 'it was much cheaper to hire you as a security guard than to find a repairman'. It was written for FNaF1, before FNaF2 existed; FNaF2's closing newspaper then has the CEO expect to reopen 'with a much smaller budget' (fnaf2-news-reopen-smaller-budget). Scott has said he did not have the whole story planned when he made the first game (scott-2018-interview-first-game-snippet-of-larger-story).

title: Scott: in FNaF2 'the old and aging animatronics are joined by a new cast'
claim: Scott's FNaF2 Steam description opens 'Welcome back' and says the old and aging animatronics are joined by a new cast of characters.
quote: In Five Nights at Freddy's 2, the old and aging animatronics are joined by a new cast of characters.
location: Five Nights at Freddy's 2 Steam store description (2014)

when.label: During FNaF2 (store text gives no date)
when.basis: Promotional text; no in-universe date

notes: Fetched from the Steam appdetails API. The text is written as if FNaF2 follows FNaF1 ('Welcome back', 'old and aging'), and the first teaser read 'Grand Reopening 2015' (scottgames-site-fnaf2-grand-reopening). Only the two checks, at the end of Night 5 and of Night 6, put the game in 1987 (fnaf2-paycheck-1987, fnaf2-overtime-robots-scrapped). On either order the older animatronics exist before the new ones. Two more records hold other sentences of this store text: scott-fnaf2-steam-description and, in the Scott file, scott-2014-fnaf2-store-previous-guard.

title: FNaF2 trailer: 'forgotten', 'dismantled', 'deactivated'
claim: Scott's official FNaF2 trailer shows the captions 'forgotten', 'dismantled' and 'deactivated' between shots of the older, damaged animatronics and the Parts & Service door, and later uses the captions 'REDESIGNED', 'REACTIVATED' and 'MALFUNCTIONING'.
quote: forgotten / dismantled / deactivated
location: Official Five Nights at Freddy's 2 trailer (Steam store page video, 2014), on-screen captions

when.label: During FNaF2 (the trailer gives no date)
when.basis: Promotional trailer; no in-universe date

notes: Captions read from frames of the trailer as hosted on Steam (app 332800, 'Game Trailer'). The first three are shown one at a time between shots of the faceless older Bonnie, a door marked 'Parts & Service', and the older Chica and Freddy. Which captions apply to which cast is a matter of placement only. The trailer also carries a short Phone Guy line, which the wiki transcribes as 'if you're hearing this, then chances are you've made a very poor career choice'; that wording was not checked here.

title: FNaF3 trailer: 'He will come back. He always does. We have a place for him.'
claim: Scott's official FNaF3 trailer shows three captions in turn: 'He will come back.', 'He always does.' and 'We have a place for him.'
quote: He will come back. He always does. We have a place for him.
location: Official Five Nights at Freddy's 3 trailer (Steam store page video, 2015), on-screen captions

when.label: During FNaF3 (30 years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed)
when.basis: Scott's FNaF3 Steam description: 'Thirty years after Freddy Fazbear's Pizza closed it's doors'

notes: Captions read from frames of the trailer as hosted on Steam (app 354140, 'Game Trailer'). 'He will come back.' is followed by the attraction's corridors, 'He always does.' by a row of the old animatronics' heads, and 'We have a place for him.' by Springtrap seated in the dark.
